holidays.name: National Catfish Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the whiskered, bottom-dwelling fish that has fed generations of Americans, especially in the South. Celebrate by frying, blackening, or simply admiring a catfish.
holidays.origin: Established by a 1987 presidential proclamation signed by Ronald Reagan, in recognition of the U.S. farm-raised catfish industry and its economic importance.
holidays.funFact: Catfish have taste buds all over their bodies, with some species having over 100,000 of them, so they essentially taste with their whole skin.

holidays.name: Take Your Dog to Work Day
holidays.description: A day when employees are encouraged to bring their canine pals to the office, turning meetings into impromptu petting sessions and spreadsheets into chew-toy zones.
holidays.origin: Created in 1996 by Pet Sitters International to celebrate dogs as companions and to encourage pet adoption. It is observed on the Friday following Father's Day, so the date shifts each year, and it falls in the same week as June 25 in many years.
holidays.funFact: Studies suggest having a dog at the workplace can lower employee stress levels throughout the day compared with workplaces without pets.

holidays.name: Global Beatles Day
holidays.description: Fans around the world celebrate the Fab Four by playing their music, hosting sing-alongs, and wearing mop-top wigs with pride.
holidays.origin: It marks the anniversary of the Beatles performing 'All You Need Is Love' on June 25, 1967, in the first live global television broadcast, Our World, which reached an estimated 400 million viewers.
holidays.funFact: The 'All You Need Is Love' broadcast included a crowd of famous friends singing along in the studio, including members of the Rolling Stones and Eric Clapton.

holidays.name: Log Cabin Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate rustic log cabins, with historic cabins opening their doors to visitors, and fans of cozy woodland living getting to feel extra smug.
holidays.origin: Observed in various places, with a long tradition in Ohio and other states, to celebrate the pioneer-era building style and the history of early settlers.
holidays.funFact: Log cabins are widely believed to have been introduced to North America by Swedish and Finnish settlers in the Delaware Valley in the 1600s.

holidays.name: National Strawberry Parfait Day
holidays.description: A layered celebration of strawberries, cream, and crunchy granola or cookie crumbles, served in a tall glass so everyone can admire the structure before wrecking it with a spoon.
holidays.origin: A modern food-day observance popularized by dessert lovers and social media calendars, with no single official founder.
holidays.funFact: The word 'parfait' is French for 'perfect', which is a bold claim for a dessert that is mostly yogurt and berries, but it holds up.
